messages:
alex: Quick check — we need a concrete proposal for how hosted/dedicated/private advertise per-tenant routing and feature gates to the edge proxy. RFC mentioned a capability registry but ops needs explicit keys they can match on.
maya: Can you sketch what fields ops needs? is this for routing only or also for QoS/eviction policies?
sam: Mostly routing + preferred model family + allowed quantization tiers. Also a flag for 'sensitive-data' that toggles private-only paths.
jing: Agree. Ops needs stable header keys and a discovery payload so proxies can make decisions without calling control plane on every request.
alex: Sketch proposal: tenant manifest advertises a small static JSON blob at attach-time, plus short-lived tokens for dynamic overrides. Example payload (kept tiny):
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "t123",
  "routing_prefs": ["hosted:low-latency","dedicated:reserved"],
  "model_whitelist": ["open-8b","rw-3b-q4"],
  "quantization_allow": ["q4_0","q8_0"],
  "sensitive_data": false
}
```
maya: Where does that live? control plane catalog + a signed `X-Redwood-Tenant-Manifest` header? proxies can trust header signature.
sam: Header size matters. Maybe manifest is stored in SSM-like store and proxies get a small id + signature: `X-RW-Tenant-Manifest-Id: mf_123` and `X-RW-Manifest-Sig: ...` then fetch is optional.
jing: For private deployments we can't assume shared fetch endpoints. We should allow the manifest to be embedded in the instance config at deploy time for private mode.
alex: Right — design constraints by mode: hosted = dynamic registry + signed headers; dedicated = registry per-cluster with local cache; private = local bundle on deploy. We need deterministic conflict resolution when both manifest and runtime override exist. Proposal: runtime overrides (explicit API calls) beat manifest, but only for non-security fields; sensitive_data is immutable after deploy unless rekeyed.
sam: How do we express gradable QoS levels? numeric priority? explicit buckets?
maya: Keep it simple: `latency_profile: "low|balanced|cost"` and `eviction_tier: "tier1|tier2|spillover"`. Proxy logic maps buckets to queues.
jing: Also add `model_fallback_order` list for safe fallthroughs.
alex: Good. We should document exact header names and a tiny JSON Schema + signing algorithm so infra teams can implement it. I'll draft a tiny RFC snippet and ping infra for review.
deploy-bot: Deploy checklist updated: add `tenant-manifest-schema-v1` to infra-radar and schedule a canary test on staging. :white_check_mark:
maya: One more operational note — telemetry: proxy should emit a `manifest_id` tag so we can trace routing decisions back to a tenant manifest.
alex: Agreed. Action items: (1) alex to drop schema + signing proto, (2) sam to prototype header+id flow on proxy, (3) jing to capture private-deploy bundle constraints. Back in 48h.
maya: Sounds good.
